trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00, take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way, book in advance for best price) to Banff town. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge (~90 min transfer). Drop bags and take a leisurely stroll down Banff Avenue to get oriented, browse the shops, and soak in the mountain atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up to the free Bow River Falls viewpoint (15-min walk from downtown) for a stunning first look at the Rockies. Watch the sunset over Tunnel Mountain from the riverside trail — completely free and breathtaking.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Calgary Airport before boarding or en route. Tim Hortons in the airport is budget-friendly (~$10-12 CAD).
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Bear Street — plant-forward menu with affordable options (~$15-20 CAD per person). Great casual spot to fuel up after travel.

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a free National Parks Day Pass or confirm your Parks Canada pass before leaving Calgary — you'll need it for most sites. Download the AllTrails app and the Parks Canada app for free trail maps. Stock up on snacks and water at the Banff IGA grocery store tonight to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early start — take the free Roam Transit Bus Route 8X (Banff to Lake Louise, ~$10 CAD each way) departing by 7:30 AM to beat the crowds. Begin the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike, walking the iconic flat lakeshore trail around turquoise Lake Louise with jaw-dropping views of Victoria Glacier. The full loop is approximately 4 km and takes 1-1.5 hours at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the lakeshore, hike up to the Lake Agnes Teahouse via the Lake Agnes Trail (7 km round trip, moderate, ~350 m elevation gain). The teahouse serves tea and simple snacks — a beloved Banff tradition. Budget for a tea and scone (~$10-15 CAD) as a mid-hike treat. Return to the lakeshore and catch the Roam Bus back toward town.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 5:30-6:00 PM. Relax at the hotel, freshen up, and take an evening walk along the Bow River Trail — a flat, peaceful path through the forest right in town.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a packed breakfast from your grocery haul — instant oatmeal, granola bars, fruit. Eat at the hotel before departing.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the IGA: sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit eaten trailside at Lake Agnes (~$8-10 CAD). Supplement with a tea at the Lake Agnes Teahouse.
meals.dinner: Subway on Banff Avenue (~$12-15 CAD) or pick up groceries for a self-catered dinner at the lodge to save budget for bigger days ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Roam Bus tickets online in advance if possible. Arrive at the Lake Louise bus stop early — this route fills up fast in July. Wear layers as mornings at Lake Louise can be cool even in summer. Sunscreen and bug spray are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Rise very early (5:30-6:00 AM departure) for Moraine Lake — Parks Canada requires visitors to take the Roam Transit Route 10S shuttle from Lake Louise Park & Ride (~$8 CAD return) as private vehicles are restricted in peak season. Arrive at Moraine Lake and immediately hike the Rockpile Trail (1.6 km, easy, 30 min) for the legendary Valley of the Ten Peaks panorama — arguably the most iconic view in Canada. The early morning light on the lake is absolutely magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue with the Moraine Lake Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return, easy, flat) hugging the impossibly blue glacial lakeshore. Explore the boulder-strewn shoreline and enjoy the stunning reflections of the Ten Peaks. Take the shuttle back to Lake Louise Park & Ride, then the Route 8X Roam Bus back to Banff town by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free Banff Visitor Centre to learn about local wildlife and geology. Walk up to Surprise Corner viewpoint (free, 10-min walk from downtown) for classic golden-hour photos of the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel framed by the Bow Valley.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast at the hotel — energy bars, bananas, and instant coffee. No time to spare on this day!
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial trailside lunch from the IGA: wraps, cheese, nuts, and chocolate (~$8-10 CAD). Eat at the Moraine Lake lakeshore.
meals.dinner: Bear Street Tavern — casual pub with shareable flatbreads and burgers, reasonably priced for Banff (~$18-22 CAD per person). Well deserved after a big hiking day.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle reservations are MANDATORY in peak season — book on the Parks Canada reservation system as far ahead as possible, as spots sell out weeks in advance. This is the most logistically important booking of the trip. Bring a warm layer; the lake sits at 1,885 m elevation and mornings can be chilly.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Icewalk — take the Roam Transit Route 9 (Banff to Johnston Canyon, ~$6 CAD each way) departing by 8:00 AM. Hike the Johnston Canyon Trail (5.1 km return, easy-moderate) through narrow limestone gorges on elevated steel catwalk platforms. Pass the dramatic Lower Falls (1.1 km) and continue to the spectacular Upper Falls (2.7 km). The canyon walls, rushing water, and carved gorges are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue past the Upper Falls on the Ink Pots Trail (additional 3 km each way, moderate) to reach the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs that bubble up in vivid green and blue pools on an open meadow with stunning mountain views. This extension is free, uncrowded, and absolutely worth it. Return via the same trail and catch the Roam Bus back to Banff.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Banff Central Park along the Bow River — a lovely free green space in town. If budget allows, treat yourself to a scoop at Cows Ice Cream on Banff Avenue (~$6-8 CAD) — a beloved Canadian institution.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the Ink Pots meadow — pack sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit from the IGA (~$8 CAD). One of the most scenic lunch spots of the trip.
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — lively brewpub with hearty pub fare. Happy hour deals on appetizers and local craft beer (~$18-22 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is one of the most popular trails in Banff — going early on the Roam Bus is key to avoiding crowds. The canyon catwalks can be slippery; wear proper hiking shoes. The Ink Pots extension adds about 2-2.5 hours but is highly recommended — the meadow is peaceful and the springs are surreal.

day_by_day.morning: Hike Tunnel Mountain — Banff's most accessible summit hike, trailhead is a 15-minute walk from downtown (completely free, no transit needed). The trail is 4.8 km return with 300 m elevation gain and takes about 2 hours. The summit offers a 360-degree panorama of the Bow Valley, the town of Banff, and the surrounding peaks — one of the best views in the area for minimal effort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Banff townsite on foot. Visit the free Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (free on Sunday afternoons for Alberta residents, otherwise ~$10 CAD) for fascinating local history and art. Walk across the bridge to Bow Falls (free) — a wide, powerful waterfall just minutes from downtown that most tourists miss. Stroll the Vermilion Lakes Drive (3 km, flat, free) for wildlife spotting — elk, beaver, and waterfowl are commonly seen here.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Vermilion Lakes — stay until golden hour for the famous reflection of Mount Rundle in the lakes. This is one of the most photographed sunset spots in Banff and it costs absolutely nothing. Return to the hotel for a relaxed final evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — yogurt, granola, and fruit purchased from IGA.
meals.lunch: Picnic at the Tunnel Mountain summit or Vermilion Lakes. Pack wraps and snacks from your grocery supply (~$6-8 CAD).
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer final dinner at The Bison Restaurant — farm-to-table Canadian cuisine with a warm mountain atmosphere. Budget around $25-30 CAD per person for a main and drink. Worth the splurge on your last full evening.

day_by_day.notes: Tunnel Mountain is an excellent option for a rest-legs day that still delivers big views. Keep eyes open for elk on the Vermilion Lakes road — they are frequently spotted at dusk. Bring a light jacket for the lake as evenings can cool down quickly even in July.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last hike or nature walk before checkout. The Marsh Loop Trail at the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (3 km, flat, free trail access) offers a peaceful boardwalk through wetlands with mountain views and resident fish in the thermal springs. Alternatively, revisit the Bow River Trail for a quiet farewell stroll through the pines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge. Store luggage at the hotel if needed. Grab a final coffee and pastry on Banff Avenue. Browse the Banff Farmers Market (seasonal, check local listings) or pick up any last souvenirs. Board the Banff Airporter shuttle back to Calgary Airport with plenty of time for your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary or onward travel. Reflect on an incredible week in the Canadian Rockies!

meals.breakfast: Wild Flour Bakery on Bear Street — Banff's best local bakery with fresh pastries, coffee, and breakfast sandwiches (~$10-14 CAD). A perfect final morning treat.
meals.lunch: Quick and budget-friendly farewell lunch at Subway or a grab-and-go wrap from IGA before the shuttle (~$10-12 CAD).
meals.dinner: Airport dining in Calgary or en route home.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Airporter return shuttle in advance to guarantee your seat — the shuttle fills up on summer Mondays. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the transfer and airport check-in. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and accommodation): ~$300-400 CAD for 6 days covering transit, park passes, meals, and activities — very achievable with grocery shopping and Roam Transit use.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary International Airport to Banff (~1.5 hours by shuttle or rental car). Enjoy the scenic drive through the foothills as you enter Banff National Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented — browse the shops, pick up a National Park pass if needed, and walk down to the Bow River Bridge for your first stunning mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Walk to Central Park along the Bow River for a relaxed introduction to the town and surrounding peaks. Enjoy a casual welcome dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the Calgary airport before or during your journey.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite at a café or deli in Banff upon arrival — try Whitebark Café for sandwiches and coffee.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace — a mid-range Banff favourite featuring locally sourced Canadian cuisine with a cozy mountain atmosphere. Budget ~$35–50 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Parks Canada Discovery Pass upon arrival if you don't already have one (~$145 CAD/adult for annual pass or $24/day). The Banff Roam Transit bus is a cost-effective way to get around town. Rest well — big hiking days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Early start to Moraine Lake and Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. Depart by 7:00 AM — Moraine Lake Road requires a Parks Canada shuttle reservation or early arrival to avoid road closures. Hike the Rockpile Trail (short but iconic, 20-minute return) for the legendary panoramic view of the ten peaks reflected in the turquoise lake. Then continue on the Lakeshore Trail (~3.4 km one way) for a serene walk along the water's edge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Moraine Lake area and enjoy lunch with the view. Optionally rent a canoe at Moraine Lake Lodge (~$110 CAD/hour) for a memorable paddle on the vivid blue water. Head back toward Lake Louise village by early afternoon and explore the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike — walk the flat, paved shoreline trail (~4 km return) in front of the iconic Fairmont Chateau with the Victoria Glacier as your backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff (45-minute drive). Relax at the hotel before heading out for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast from the hotel or grab a takeaway from Evelyn's Coffee Bar in Banff before departing. Bring trail snacks and water.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at Moraine Lake — sandwiches, fruit, and trail mix. There is a small café at Moraine Lake Lodge as a backup (~$20–30 CAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tooloulou's in Banff — a lively Cajun-inspired restaurant with generous portions and mid-range pricing (~$25–40 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Parks Canada Moraine Lake shuttle well in advance (opens for reservations months ahead). Shuttles depart from Banff or Lake Louise. Bring layers — mornings at elevation can be cool even in July. Sunscreen and bug spray recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Icewalk — depart Banff by 8:30 AM for the 25-minute drive to Johnston Canyon trailhead. Walk the dramatic canyon trail along elevated metal catwalk bridges bolted into the canyon walls. Visit the Lower Falls (~1.1 km one way) and Upper Falls (~2.7 km one way), passing through narrow limestone gorges carved by the rushing Johnston Creek. The cool canyon air makes this a refreshing morning hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue past the Upper Falls to the Ink Pots — seven cold-water mineral springs that bubble up in vivid green and blue pools in an open meadow (~5.8 km one way from trailhead). This extends the hike to a full half-day adventure with stunning views of the surrounding peaks. Return to the trailhead and drive back to Banff.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Banff. Visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$18 CAD per person) for a well-deserved soak in natural mineral waters with mountain views — a perfect way to soothe tired hiking muscles.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Cows Banff (opens early) — known for hearty breakfast options and famous ice cream. Budget ~$12–18 CAD.
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch again for the canyon hike. Alternatively, grab food at the Johnston Canyon Resort café near the trailhead (~$15–25 CAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Park Distillery Restaurant + Bar on Banff Avenue — Canadian comfort food made with local ingredients, craft cocktails and spirits distilled in-house. Budget ~$30–45 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is one of Banff's most popular trails — going early helps beat the crowds. The canyon walls keep this trail shaded and cool, so a light jacket is recommended even on warm days. The Ink Pots extension adds ~6 km round trip but is well worth it for the payoff.

day_by_day.morning: Banff Gondola and Sulphur Mountain Summit Hike — choose to hike the 5.5 km Sulphur Mountain Trail (allow ~2 hours up, moderate difficulty, 655 m elevation gain) for a rewarding climb through subalpine forest with increasingly spectacular views. At the summit (2,281 m), explore the 1 km summit boardwalk connecting Sulphur and Sanson Peaks with 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the gondola back down (included with hiking ticket or purchase a one-way gondola descent ticket ~$35 CAD). After descending, visit the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (~$8 CAD) — the birthplace of Canada's national park system, where warm sulphur springs emerge from the earth. Explore the interpretive exhibits and the outdoor boardwalk over the historic basin.
day_by_day.evening: Canoe Rental on the Bow River — rent a canoe from Banff Canoe Club (open until early evening in summer, ~$50–65 CAD/hour for a canoe). Paddle the calm, glacier-fed Bow River through the heart of Banff with Tunnel Mountain and the surrounding peaks reflected in the glassy water. A magical golden-hour experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. Fuel up well before the Sulphur Mountain hike.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Sky Bistro at the top of the Banff Gondola — a sit-down restaurant at the summit with spectacular views. Mid-range pricing (~$25–40 CAD for a meal). A special treat with an unforgettable backdrop.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse on Banff Avenue — a Banff institution for quality Alberta beef steaks and sharing plates in a lively atmosphere. Budget ~$40–60 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Banff Gondola tickets online in advance to secure your preferred time slot and avoid queues. If hiking up, start by 8:00–9:00 AM to have time for the summit boardwalk before it gets crowded. Banff Canoe Club is a short walk from downtown — no advance booking typically required but go early in the evening for the best light.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93) — one of the world's most scenic drives. Head north from Banff toward the Columbia Icefield (~2 hours). Stop at Bow Lake (stunning turquoise glacial lake, short shoreline walk) and Peyto Lake viewpoint (a short 1.1 km hike to an iconic wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake overlook — one of the most spectacular views in the Rockies).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre. Walk the free Toe of the Athabasca Glacier Trail (~1.5 km return) to get up close to the ancient glacier. Optionally book the Glacier Adventure (Ice Explorer bus onto the glacier, ~$65 CAD) or Glacier Skywalk (~$35 CAD) for an enhanced experience. Begin the scenic drive back south through the Parkway, stopping at Mistaya Canyon (short 900 m walk to a dramatic narrow canyon) on the return.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed final full-day evening with a walk along the Bow River Pathway before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing. Pack snacks and water for the full day drive.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Icefield Centre cafeteria or packed lunch from the hotel. The cafeteria offers soups, sandwiches and hot meals (~$15–25 CAD). Eating on the parkway is part of the adventure.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nourish Bistro — a popular mid-range vegetarian and vegan restaurant in Banff with creative, wholesome dishes. A great lighter option after a big day. Budget ~$25–40 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up on gas in Banff before heading out — fuel is limited and expensive along the Icefields Parkway. Start early (7:30–8:00 AM) to make the most of the day and beat crowds at Peyto Lake. Wildlife sightings (elk, bears, bighorn sheep) are common along the Parkway — keep a safe distance and carry bear spray on any walks.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning hike — Tunnel Mountain Summit Trail, departing from near the hotel. A short but rewarding hike (2.3 km one way, ~300 m elevation gain, allow 1–1.5 hours up) with panoramic views over the Bow Valley, the town of Banff, and the surrounding peaks. A perfect final morning activity that's accessible right from town without a car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and enjoy a leisurely last afternoon. Browse the Banff shops along Banff Avenue for souvenirs and local goods. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (~$10 CAD) for an interesting look at the cultural and natural history of the region. Pack up and check out from Banff Mountain Lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Banff before heading to Calgary for departure (or overnight in Calgary if flying out the next day). Scenic drive back through the mountains as the sun sets over the Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Sit-down farewell breakfast at the hotel or at Melissa's Missteak — a beloved Banff breakfast institution with hearty portions and a cozy log cabin atmosphere. Budget ~$15–22 CAD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Bear Street Tavern — great wood-fired pizzas and casual atmosphere, perfect for a relaxed last afternoon. Budget ~$20–30 CAD.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The Maple Leaf Grille & Lounge on Banff Avenue — upscale Canadian cuisine featuring Alberta beef, wild salmon and local game in an elegant but accessible setting. A memorable send-off. Budget ~$45–65 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 1.5–2 hours to drive from Banff to Calgary International Airport, plus time for fuel and car return. If your flight is early the next morning, consider booking a Calgary hotel for the night. Double-check Parks Canada shuttle reservations and any activity bookings have been cancelled or used. Take one last look at the mountains — you'll want to come back!

Take a leisurely self-guided stroll along the Bow River Promenade through downtown Banff to acclimate to the mountain air and soak in the stunning Rockies backdrop. Browse the boutiques along Banff Avenue at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Canoe Rental on Bow River – As the afternoon light softens into golden hour, enjoy a private guided canoe experience on the calm, glacier-fed Bow River. Glide past wildlife-rich riverbanks with the iconic mountain peaks reflected on the water. A perfect, gentle introduction to Banff's natural splendour.

meals.lunch: Grab a premium bite at the Calgary airport or enjoy snacks provided by your private transfer service en route to Banff.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant, Banff – A Banff institution offering refined Canadian cuisine featuring Alberta bison, wild salmon, and locally foraged ingredients. Extensive Canadian wine and whisky selection. Reservation recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury transfer from Calgary International Airport in advance (e.g., Banff Airporter VIP or a private car service). Tip: The Bow River canoe experience is best enjoyed between 17:00–19:00 for golden-hour lighting and calmer winds. Pack a light layer as temperatures can drop near the river in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake and Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek – Depart early (07:00) to beat the crowds at one of Canada's most breathtaking landscapes. Hike the Rockpile Trail for the iconic panoramic view over Moraine Lake and the ten soaring peaks, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail hugging the vivid turquoise water's edge. The early morning light on the peaks is extraordinary. Note: Private vehicle access or pre-booked shuttle is required as personal vehicles are restricted.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning trek, return to Banff for a relaxed afternoon. Indulge in a signature treatment at the Willow Stream Spa at the Fairmont Banff Springs – choose from mountain-inspired therapies such as the Rocky Mountain Journey body wrap or a deep-tissue massage. A perfect recovery after the morning hike.
day_by_day.evening: Banff Gondola and Sulphur Mountain Sunset – Take the Banff Gondola to the summit at 2,281 metres for a spectacular sunset over the Rockies. Walk the summit boardwalk to Sanson's Peak and enjoy 360-degree panoramic views as the sky turns amber and pink over the mountain ranges.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Banff Mountain Lodge before 07:00 departure – request a packed premium breakfast or enjoy the lodge's morning spread.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch with gourmet provisions prepared by the lodge or a local deli (e.g., Nourish Bistro or Evelyn's Coffee Bar) enjoyed at the Moraine Lake lakeshore.
meals.dinner: Sky Bistro at the top of the Banff Gondola – Dine above the clouds with panoramic mountain views. Upscale Canadian menu featuring Alberta beef tenderloin, trout, and seasonal ingredients. Pair your meal with a curated selection from their impressive wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake access: Book the Parks Canada shuttle or a private tour well in advance as access is highly restricted and fills up months ahead. Bring sunscreen, hiking poles, and layers. The Willow Stream Spa at Fairmont Banff Springs requires advance booking – reserve before your trip. Combine gondola visit with dinner reservation at Sky Bistro for a seamless, premium evening experience.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike – Drive or take a private transfer to the iconic Lake Louise (approximately 45 minutes from Banff). Arrive by 08:00 to experience the serene emerald-green lake before day-trippers arrive. Walk the full shoreline trail around the lake, with the Victoria Glacier towering at the far end. The reflections of the surrounding peaks on the glassy water are utterly mesmerizing. Extend the walk up to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse trail for added elevation and drama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Lake Louise area further with a visit to the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise for afternoon tea in their elegant Lakeview Lounge, gazing directly onto the lake. Alternatively, rent a premium canoe directly on Lake Louise for a unique on-water perspective of the surrounding peaks and glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail at the Grizzly House or the Banff Ave Brewing Co. rooftop patio, then head to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise – The Fairview Bar & Restaurant offers a sumptuous breakfast with floor-to-ceiling lake views. A truly world-class dining setting.
meals.lunch: Afternoon tea or light lunch at the Lakeview Lounge, Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise – finger sandwiches, house-baked scones, and premium loose-leaf teas with a direct view of the lake.
meals.dinner: Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel, Banff – Banff's most acclaimed fine-dining destination. Award-winning contemporary cuisine with an extraordinary wine cellar. Multi-course tasting menus with wine pairing available. Dress code applies.

day_by_day.notes: Lake Louise parking is extremely limited in summer – a private transfer or pre-booked shuttle is strongly recommended. Canoe rentals on Lake Louise are available directly from the Fairmont boathouse and should be reserved in advance. Bring a camera with a wide-angle lens – the morning light on the lake is exceptional for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Icewalk – Embark on one of Banff's most dramatic canyon experiences. Follow the suspended catwalk trail through a narrow limestone gorge carved by Johnston Creek, passing the thundering Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). The canyon walls rise dramatically overhead and the mist from the falls is refreshing on a warm summer day. For the premium experience, book a guided interpretive tour to learn about the canyon's geology and ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff and spend the afternoon at leisure. Visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a soak in the naturally heated mineral waters with panoramic mountain views – a wonderfully restorative experience. Follow up with another session at the Willow Stream Spa or simply relax on the lodge's terrace with a glass of local craft beer or wine.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or walk along the Tunnel Mountain Trail (2.7 km loop from town) for sweeping views over the Bow Valley and town of Banff at dusk. A short, accessible hike perfect for a relaxed evening with spectacular views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Banff Mountain Lodge – Enjoy a full hot breakfast at the lodge before departing for Johnston Canyon.
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Trout House at Storm Mountain Lodge (en route back from Johnston Canyon) – a rustic-chic log cabin restaurant serving elevated Canadian comfort food in an intimate, heritage setting.
meals.dinner: Saltlik Steakhouse, Banff – A premier steakhouse celebrating Alberta's world-renowned beef. Prime AAA Alberta steaks, dry-aged cuts, and an extensive wine list. Perfect for a hearty dinner after a full day of hiking.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is very popular on weekends – arrive by 08:30 to avoid crowds. Wear waterproof shoes or trail runners as the canyon trail can be wet and slippery near the falls. The Banff Upper Hot Springs are open daily and bathing suits can be rented on-site. Tunnel Mountain Trail is dog-friendly and ideal for a gentle evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Banff Gondola and Sulphur Mountain Summit Hike (Hiking Option) – For a more active experience, hike the 5.5 km Sulphur Mountain Trail from the Banff Hot Springs trailhead to the summit at 2,281 metres. The trail gains approximately 655 metres in elevation through dense subalpine forest, opening up to breathtaking panoramic views at the top. Take the gondola back down and enjoy the summit boardwalk at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic Icefields Parkway Drive – Hire a private driver or luxury vehicle and embark on a curated afternoon drive along a section of the legendary Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), one of the world's most scenic roads. Stop at Bow Lake, Peyto Lake Viewpoint (a vivid turquoise wolf-head-shaped lake), and the Crowfoot Glacier Viewpoint. The scenery is otherworldly and constantly changing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a premium farewell-style evening. Enjoy cocktails at the bar of the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel – even if not staying there, the iconic castle hotel's bar is a quintessential Banff experience. Watch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks from the hotel's terrace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Crave Mountain Grill or the lodge restaurant – fuel up with a protein-rich breakfast before the summit hike.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch to enjoy at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake during the Icefields Parkway drive. Arrange with the lodge or a local gourmet provisioner the evening before.
meals.dinner: 1888 Chop House at the Fairmont Banff Springs – A legendary fine-dining steakhouse within the iconic Banff Springs castle. Exceptional Alberta prime beef, seafood, and an award-winning wine program. One of Banff's most celebrated dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: The Sulphur Mountain hike is moderately challenging – allow 2–2.5 hours up and take the gondola down (gondola ticket required for descent). The Icefields Parkway afternoon drive covers approximately 100–150 km return depending on your chosen stops – a private driver allows you to focus entirely on the scenery. Book the 1888 Chop House reservation well in advance, especially for a Saturday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning Nature Walk – Rise early for one last immersion in Banff's natural beauty. Take a peaceful walk along the Vermilion Lakes Drive (flat, accessible, 5 km return) at the edge of town. The three shallow lakes are a haven for wildlife including elk, beavers, osprey, and herons. The still morning water reflects the surrounding peaks perfectly – a serene and memorable final experience in the Rockies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge and depart for Calgary International Airport via private luxury transfer. The drive takes approximately 1.5 hours. Stop briefly at the viewpoint at the eastern entrance of Banff National Park for a final look back at the mountains. Arrive at the airport with ample time for your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or overnight in Calgary if flight schedule requires.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the Banff Mountain Lodge – savour a full lodge breakfast and take in the mountain views one last time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Tooloulou's or Coyotes Southwestern Grill in Banff town before checkout, or enjoy premium airport dining at Calgary International.
meals.dinner: If departing late or overnighting in Calgary: Dinner at CHARCUT Roast House in downtown Calgary – a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant known for its whole-animal butchery, house-cured charcuterie, and Alberta-sourced ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Vermilion Lakes is best visited at sunrise or early morning for wildlife sightings and mirror-like reflections – bring binoculars and a camera. Confirm private transfer pickup time the evening before to ensure a smooth checkout and airport transfer. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Calgary International. Purchase any last-minute souvenirs in Banff town before departing.

query: Banff hiking and lakes, $2800 couple, 6 days, July 2027, from Calgary
